title: Observability privacy gateway for traces and metrics
creator: Lena Thompson
description: Add a lightweight privacy gateway in front of the observability ingestion pipeline to enforce tenant-scoped PII attenuation, dynamic retention, and access controls for traces, metrics labels, and logs. The gateway should be pluggable into both hosted and private deployments and support runtime policies per tenant and per dataset. This ticket covers design, a proof-of-concept filter, and an initial canary rollout behind a feature flag.
background: Incidents and audits over the last 12 months revealed inconsistent handling of sensitive identifiers in trace spans and metric labels across services. Current scrubbing hooks are decentralized and incomplete. We need a centralized, low-latency enforcement layer that standardizes attenuation (redaction, truncation, tokenization) and retention gates while preserving cardinality/observability for SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: A privacy gateway component exists that can be inserted into the ingestion path for traces and metric label pipelines
Gateway applies tenant-configurable attenuation rules (redact, truncate, tokenize) to span attributes and metric labels
End-to-end ingestion latency increase at p95 stays below 2% for standard workloads in canary tests
Per-tenant retention windows are enforced and visible in ingest telemetry
Gateway emits an immutable access-log event for any raw-field access with requester identity and justification
RBAC checks block query-level access to redacted fields and are integrated with existing console roles
Feature is behind a runtime feature flag and can be rolled back without data loss
implementation_notes: Design gateway as a stateless filter service that can be horizontally scaled and placed before Kafka/streams ingestion
Reuse existing tracing hook interfaces where available; add a light-weight SDK shim for services that can't update hooks immediately
Implement attenuation strategies: full redaction (remove key), truncation (length safe), tokenization with reversible token store behind KMS for JIT access
Metric label scrubber should optionally drop high-cardinality labels and emit a renormalized label with _redacted suffix
Retention enforcement: gateway tags records with tenant retention_ttl and a 'garbage_collect_after' metadata field interpreted by downstream retention worker
Access logging: structured event sent to an audit topic with tenant_id, requestor, field_path, policy_id, timestamp
RBAC integration: consult central RBAC service on admin-level queries; add per-route policy cache with 1 minute TTL
Performance budget: prefer fast, deterministic operations; avoid expensive crypto on hot path except JIT decryption behind gated endpoints
rollout_plan: 1) Merge POC behind feature flag. 2) Run internal canary in staging with synthetic high-cardinality trace traffic. 3) Enable for a single low-risk tenant for 48h and monitor SLOs. 4) Gradual ramp to 10% of inbound traffic over 72h with telemetry checks. 5) Full rollout and enable retention enforcement. Rollback path: feature flag off and downstream workers ignore retention tags until GC window elapses.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased ingestion latency under burst. Mitigation: autoscale gateway replicas and implement fast-path no-op when policy is empty.
Risk: Loss of cardinality causing alert noise. Mitigation: provide renormalized labels and retain a sampled raw span for troubleshooting (sampled storage with strict retention).
Risk: Improper token store configuration could leak reversible tokens. Mitigation: require KMS-backed store and automated key-rotation reviews as part of deployment.
Risk: RBAC mismatches preventing legitimate access. Mitigation: provide a policy dry-run mode and admin override with audit trail for early rollout.
Risk: Backwards compatibility with on-prem customers. Mitigation: configurable deployment hooks and an opt-in migration guide for private deployments.
test_plan: Unit tests for attenuation strategies and policy engine
Load test with synthetic traces matching production cardinality profile
Chaos tests that kill gateway pods and validate graceful degradation and no data corruption
End-to-end canary smoke that verifies retention TTLs and audit event emission
Integration tests for RBAC checks against staging identity provider
